newsitem.title: GERMANY: German CSU tells France not to seek soft EMU.
newsitem.headline: German CSU tells France not to seek soft EMU.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU) party issued a stern warning on Wednesday to France not to seek a watering-down of entry criteria for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).

The warning comes a week after Waigel had to step in to quell rumours that the CSU, a core part of the German coalition government, would push for an outright delay of EMU following the election of the Socialists in France.

"The Socialist government in Paris must realise there can be no softening of the Maastricht criteria (for EMU entry) nor shift away from existing treaty pacts," CSU parliamentary Michael Glos said in the Bayernkurier party newspaper.

Glos said this applied particularly to the so-called stability pact, a Waigel initiative designed to ensure the future stability of the euro by censuring EMU participants whose economies fail to meet agreed performance targets.
The new left-wing French government was elected on promises to reorient the push towards EMU away from its current austerity-based course towards a jobs and economic growth focus.

Paris earlier this week caused alarm, particularly in Germany, by saying it might not be ready to ratify the stability pact at next week's EU summit. It has since indicated it may yet be able to agree to the pact in time.
Waigel will next week lay out his plans for ensuring Germany will meet convergence criteria for EMU at a meeting of CSU members.

CSU sources in Bavaria's state parliament have said there is broad dissatisfaction with Waigel in his own party, particularly after his attempt to revalue Bundesbank assets, a plan which smacked too much of "creative accounting" for some in the CSU. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
